ai_catalog.name: rag_example_app
ai_catalog.rough_description: Takes a natural-language question plus a small public dataset and produces a generated answer grounded in retrieved passages from that dataset, illustrating the RAG pattern end-to-end.
ai_catalog.tier_decision_rationale: The whole point of this example is to illustrate the use of RAG, so the retrieval pipeline is intentional despite the small dataset size.

ai_catalog.name: custom_text_semantic_placement
ai_catalog.rough_description: Takes a user-entered custom word, phrase, or sentence and produces its semantic position relative to the curated preset examples in the shared 2D visualization, letting users see how their own text clusters with (or diverges from) existing categories and sentences.

ai_catalog.name: single_call_generation
ai_catalog.rough_description: Takes a user-entered or preset prompt and returns either a plain-text response or a JSON-schema-conforming structured response depending on the selected mode, demonstrating a single direct LLM call with no retrieval or chaining.

ai_catalog.name: chained_role_play_generation
ai_catalog.rough_description: Takes a user's free-form story prompt and produces two sequential, role-conditioned outputs (a short story from a 'struggling writer' persona, then a critique from a 'harsh critic' persona reacting to that story) — both shown to the user. Requires generation because the story and critique content must be composed in natural language conditioned on persona and prior output, not looked up or computed.

ai_catalog.name: trip_day_planning_agent
ai_catalog.rough_description: Takes a user's city and free-form interests and produces a one-day itinerary: a planner model call decomposes the fuzzy natural-language goal into a small displayed plan of research and synthesis steps, and executor model calls carry out those steps (using the shared Exa web search tool for research) to compose the final itinerary. A model is required because interpreting open-ended interests, decomposing them into a plan, grounding research in unstructured web results, and writing a coherent itinerary are semantic, generative tasks that plain code cannot perform.

ai_catalog.name: orchestrated_specialist_answer
ai_catalog.rough_description: Takes a user's preset or free-form question and returns a delegation decision (which two of the four fixed specialists were chosen, why, and the brief written for each), each specialist's answer to its brief, and a single merged final response. Demonstrates fan-out/fan-in delegation as a working, visible example. Coordinates question_moderation, specialist_disagreement_note. Depends on question_moderation.

ai_catalog.name: question_moderation
ai_catalog.rough_description: Takes a visitor's free-form question submitted to the public demo and returns whether it is safe and in scope for the knowledge-only specialists, with a short reason when it is not. Protects an unauthenticated public demo from abusive or off-topic prompts before quota is spent. Part of the orchestrated_specialist_answer capability.

ai_catalog.name: specialist_disagreement_note
ai_catalog.rough_description: Takes the two specialists' independent answers and returns a short note describing where they overlap, complement, or contradict each other, displayed alongside the merged response. Makes the educational point that independent subagents can reach differing conclusions. Part of the orchestrated_specialist_answer capability. Depends on orchestrated_specialist_answer.
